title: Santa Barbara Maritime Museum

services.name: View Exhibits
services.desc: SBMM opened its doors to the public in July 2000, with the unique mission to interpret the rich and diverse maritime history of the Santa Barbara Channel. As such, the museum has a robust collection of historical artifacts ranging from cannon balls to shipwreck materials to navy artifacts and ship models. One of the most masterful modelers of his time, Dwight Brooks created scale-model boats, ships, and planes that were fully operational. His work is familiar to readers of the old Scale Ship Modeler magazine, where several of his models appeared. services.name: Private Rentals
services.desc: The Santa Barbara Maritime Museum is a great location for any event - whether a social, private, or corporate gathering. Multiple locations exist within the museum to highlight your meeting, lecture, or event including the main floor, mezzanine (or second floor), the Munger Theater, and the fourth-floor crow’s nest. services.name: Whales Are Superheroes
services.desc: Whales help sustain the entire living system of the ocean. They have the power to inspire us to care about our oceans. Almost 30 percent of the world’s 93 whale and dolphin species have been documented in the Santa Barbara Channel, making our local waters one of the best places in the world to go whale watching. Whales have a powerful and positive influence on the function of oceans, global carbon storage, and the health of commercial fisheries. Whales serve as nutrient pumps, feasting on fish and invertebrates. Many whales release fecal matter at the surface, which fertilizes the surface of the sea.
